newsitem.title: USA: CBOT RICE ENDS LOWER ON PRE-REPORT POSITIONING.
newsitem.headline: CBOT RICE ENDS LOWER ON PRE-REPORT POSITIONING.

text.p: CBOT rice futures ended a quiet session lower on Monday amid position-squaring ahead of Tuesday's USDA crop production and supply and demand reports, traders said.
Weather was also cited as a mildly bearish factor. A heat wave that had threatened rice in the U.S. South moderated, easing concerns the crop would begin heading in hot weather.
Results of the early harvest in Louisiana were also said to be promising. One trader said yields were coming in higher than some reported very early in the harvest season.
Export talk offered a slight boost.
Traders said there were rumors Peru had bought U.S. brown rice but price and tonnage details were unavailable.
Rice ended three cents per cwt lower with September down three at $9.67. Volume was estimated by CBOT at 250 lots, compared with Friday's actual volume of 265 lots.
